body:
reproduced on three configurations (nightly 2.14.0.dev20260731+cu130 on a GTX 1660 Ti and on CPU, plus a source build of main at 21f6559 on aarch64): eager returns tensor([2.]), compiled returns a 12-element tensor of mostly uninitialized values.

I dug into the root cause. It is not functionalization: backend="aot_eager" produces the correct result, only backend="inductor" is wrong. The chain:

Dynamo graph-breaks on resize_() as documented (gb0126), so the resize_ runs in eager between two compiled graphs.
The first graph returns both base and its same-shape view, and inductor's generated wrapper returns the same tensor object for both: return (buf0, buf0, ). In eager these are distinct objects sharing one storage. A minimal probe with no resize_ at all shows it: compiling return base, alias gives base is alias == True under inductor, False in eager.
The eager-executed resize_(12) therefore resizes base itself, and the second graph is traced against the already-corrupted tensor (its generated code asserts a (12,) input).
To validate the mechanism I patched PythonWrapperCodegen.generate_return locally to wrap duplicated output refs in .view_as(...), giving each output a distinct tensor object. With that change the repro returns tensor([2.]) and matches eager on all backends.


I'd like to work on the fix. Happy to take direction on the preferred venue: deduplicating output refs in the wrapper codegen (as in my probe), emitting a proper view with explicit metadata for aliased outputs, or handling it on the AOTAutograd side with view replay. (The diagnosis also suggests module: inductor fits better than module: aotdispatch.)
For context, `resize_` is a gnarly API that is not recommended for wide usage--it is a "use at your own risk" API, so getting to landing a fix here may take a while.
